problem: Foundation-model (LLM) ObjectNav agents either prompt with unordered object lists or greedy local views, and existing scene graphs hard-code a schema for one environment type (e.g. rooms/floors). This prevents zero-shot generalisation across diverse environments, goals and robot embodiments in the open world.
motivation: Robots need to find arbitrary natural-language goals in novel environments (homes, supermarkets, offices) without maps or environment-specific engineering. LLMs hold rich semantic priors but struggle to organise and maintain spatial memory at scale, so a structured yet flexible, LLM-friendly spatial memory is needed.
key_idea: Use an Open Scene Graph, a hierarchical topo-semantic memory whose structure is defined by an LLM-generatable environment-specific schema, as the shared memory that lets LLMs, VFMs and a general navigation model (ViNT) compose into a zero-shot open-world ObjectNav system.
insight: Structured memory matters: on HM3D with GT perception, LGX-GT (greedy, no memory) gets SR 0.275, LFG-GT (object-only frontier memory) 0.675, and OSG-Nav-GT (objects + regions + topology) 0.775, and qualitative cases show region semantics and Connectors as frontiers avoid exhaustive search. Purely semantic object features are enough for LLM-based place recognition and data association (Table 6), and iterative generate-canonicalise-verify is essential for valid schemas (direct LLM prompting gave 0/10 valid schemas). Perception and LLM quality bound performance (GPT-3.5 0.693 vs LLaMA-2-7B 0.349 SR; GNM limits real-world runs).
method: OSG representation: layered heterogeneous directed graph with Object, Place, Connector and Region Abstraction nodes and edges is_near / connects_to / has / contains; nodes carry open-vocab labels, appearance descriptions and image crops; object features (lists of nearby objects) serve as landmarks
OSG schema: template (JSON/YAML) specialising the ontology for an environment type (home, supermarket, office, mall); hand-written or auto-generated by an LLM
Schema generator: 3-stage Generate-Canonicalise-Verify pipeline (long-form description, triplet extraction and canonicalisation, structural verifier with feedback) iterated until valid

Mapper: Image Parser (GroundingDINO detection, BLIP-2 VQA for place labels and object descriptions, LLM sorts detections into Objects/Connectors), State Estimator (LLM place recognition by semantic-similar place filtering plus pairwise object-feature matching), OSG Updater (LLM data association, greedy LLM abstraction into higher region layers)
Probabilistic Mapper extension: OPTM-style particle filter over map topologies with Dirichlet-process proposal and LLM-logit observation likelihood (proposed, not part of main results)

Reasoner: Region Proposer (coarse-to-fine LLM selection from top layer down to a Place), Pathfinder (Dijkstra over Place/Connector graph), Object Proposer (LLM picks objects/connectors as image subgoals, with reasoning)
Controller: ViNT general navigation model (zero-shot) conditioned on goal object image crops, stopping via a temporal-distance threshold; FMM local planner used in simulation

setting.backbone: GPT-3.5 (frozen, reasoning/mapping), GroundingDINO + BLIP-2 (frozen VFMs), ViNT (frozen GNM, real world); FMM local planner in simulation
setting.training_data: none (training-free; all foundation models used zero-shot)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB only (perception from RGB; sim baselines/variants get noiseless positioning for FMM local planner)
setting.action_space: MoveToObject/MoveToRegion primitives realised as velocity commands (real-world, ViNT) or discrete FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 30° with FMM (simulation)
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson tiny val, HM3D-Semantics v0.1) plus real world
setting.privileged: none for the main OSG-Nav (OSG-Nav-GT variant uses GT semantic annotations; hand-designed schema per environment type; environment-type label given; sim uses FMM local planner with positioning)

numbers_note: Simulation splits are named 'val' (Gibson tiny val, HM3D val); benchmark rows are the paper's own evaluation subsets. Additional rare-query (settee SR 0.8, nightstand SR 0.7) and compositional-query results are in Tables 4-5 on custom HM3D episodes, not listed.
results: OSG-Nav reaches SR 0.734 / SPL 0.386 on Gibson, competitive with the learned PONI (SR 0.736, SPL 0.410) and beating training-free SemUtil (SR 0.693, SPL 0.405) and LFG (0.645). On HM3D it gets SR 0.693 (0.775 with GT perception vs LFG-GT 0.675), and it works zero-shot on Spot and Fetch and on open-vocabulary and rare/compositional goals.
limitations: Topo-semantic only, with no explicit metric geometry, so SPL is lower than the best metric methods on HM3D (0.283 vs LFG-GT 0.389); depends on GPT-3.5 (small local LLMs are much worse) and on VFM perception errors (BLIP-2 mislabelling, GroundingDINO accuracy)
Real-world failures are mainly due to the GNM (ViNT), which gets stuck in clutter and is sensitive to camera FoV; real-world evaluation is small (5 trials per goal)
Auto-generated schemas have limited coverage (omit specialised regions or optional Connectors); only indoor environments evaluated and a given environment-type label is required
